questions.question: An article is sold at a profit of 25%. If its cost price is reduced by 20% and it is sold at the same selling price, then what will be the profit per cent?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Profit = 25%, CP is reduced = 20%

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (100 + P%)/100

Profit = SP - CP

Profit% = P × 100/CP

**Calculation:**

Let CP be Rs. 100

SP = 100 × (100 + 25)/100 = 125

If CP is reduced 20%, then CP = 80

But SP is the same i.e Rs. 125

Profit = 125 - 80 = 45

Profit% = 45 × 100/80 = ​56(1)/(4)​​%

**​∴ The profit % is 56(1)/(4)%**

questions.question: The cost price of a saree to a person X was ₹100. Person X sells the saree to person Y at a profit of 10% and person Y then sells it to person Z at a loss of 10%. How much does person Z pay for the saree?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of X = Rs100

**Concept Used:**

Final value = Initial value ( 1 + R/100) ( 1- R/100)

Where, R = increment and decrement of Rate successively

**Calculation:**

Here, we have Initial value = Cost price of X = Rs100 , Rate of increment = 10%, Rate of decrement = 10%

⇒ Final value = Initial value (1+R/100) ( 1-R/100) = 100 × ( 1 +10/100) × ( 1- 10/100) 

⇒ Final value = 100 × 11/10 × 9/10 = Rs99.

**Hence, Z pays Rs.99 for the saree.**
